active_paradigms.idea: Nelder-Mead simplex restarts on soft-min objective
active_paradigms.description: Replace simulated annealing with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='Nelder-Mead') applied to a smooth soft-min surrogate: objective = -log(sum(exp(-area_i/tau))) over all 165 triangle areas, with tau annealed from ~1e-3 to 1e-6 across restarts. Nelder-Mead needs no gradients and handles the non-smooth min well via the soft-min. Parameterize points in barycentric coordinates clipped by softmax to guarantee feasibility, so unconstrained optimization works. Run ~20 restarts from perturbed versions of the current best configuration plus random seeds, each with maxiter ~2000, keep the best true min area. This differs from failed SLSQP attempts because Nelder-Mead is derivative-free and the softmax parameterization guarantees feasibility without constraints.
active_paradigms.cautions: Evaluate true min at the end, not soft-min; keep tau small enough that soft-min tracks true min; project final points with barycentric clamp for safety.

active_paradigms.description: Use scipy.spatial.Voronoi/Delaunay structure: iteratively move each point away from the centroid of its nearest neighbors (Lloyd-like relaxation with area-aware repulsion), specifically pushing points toward underused regions where small triangles occur. Identify the ~10 smallest triangles, compute their centroids, and move their vertices along directions that increase those areas (gradient of area w.r.t. each vertex is analytic: for triangle (a,b,c), dArea/dx is a rotation of the opposite edge). Take the analytic vertex-gradient of the minimum-area triangles and do projected gradient ascent with backtracking line search — pure numpy, no scipy optimizer. This is a fundamentally different geometric-gradient method rather than stochastic or LP-based search.
active_paradigms.cautions: Use the gradient of the currently-minimal triangles only (recompute set each iteration); project back into triangle after each step; use backtracking to guarantee monotone improvement.
active_paradigms.approach_type: numpy analytic gradient ascent on minimal triangles

active_paradigms.idea: Known optimal-structure templates with coordinate refinement
active_paradigms.description: Exploit that good n=11 configurations likely have points on the boundary and structured interior placement: enumerate a small family of combinatorial templates (e.g., k points on each edge with parametrized positions plus interior points on the medians), then run coordinate-descent refinement only within each template's low-dimensional parameter space (often 5-10 free parameters instead of 22). This drastically reduces dimensionality, letting exhaustive grid + local polish find configurations the 22-D annealer misses. Different from failed symmetry-restricted search because it allows asymmetric edge distributions and many templates, not just 3-fold symmetric ones. Include templates matching the benchmark 0.03653 (score>1) if reachable: e.g., 4+4+3 edge splits with staggered interior points.
active_paradigms.cautions: Keep total templates modest to fit time budget; refine each template with the existing greedy polish; verify feasibility via barycentric projection.

tried_paradigms.idea: Maximin smooth optimization via log-sum-exp soft-min with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP)
tried_paradigms.description: Replace simulated annealing with gradient-based continuous optimization. Objective: negative log-sum-exp(-areas/temperature) over all 165 triangles — a smooth surrogate for min area. Compute areas analytically with autodiff-free hand-derived gradients or use finite differences via SLSQP. Constraints: barycentric coordinates >= 0 (linear constraints, easy for SLSQP). Anneal temperature down from ~1e-2 to ~1e-6 across restarts from multiple seeds (structured boundary + random). This directly targets the true optimum with far better convergence than random Metropolis moves.
tried_paradigms.cautions: 165 triangles × 22 variables; precompute index arrays; use barycentric parametrization so constraints are simple bounds u,v,w>=0, u+v+w=1 (reduce to 22 free vars); fall back to current SA result if SLSQP fails.

tried_paradigms.idea: LP-based maximin lower-bound search with scipy.optimize.linprog
tried_paradigms.description: At any configuration, each triangle area is a (piecewise) linear function of one point's position when others are fixed. Iteratively solve: maximize t subject to area_i >= t for all triangles, linearizing |cross| by fixing signs (signs change rarely near optimum). Use scipy.optimize.linprog per iteration over all 22 coordinates with sign-fixed linear area constraints and triangle-bound constraints; update signs and repeat. This is essentially a Goldfarb-Idnani / LP-annealing approach that converges to a KKT point of the maximin problem and can escape poor local minima found by SA. Warm-start from the current best configuration and also from symmetric structured seeds (e.g., points on 3-fold symmetric orbits).
tried_paradigms.cautions: Handle degenerate sign flips by re-checking signs after each LP solve; project results into triangle; keep SA fallback for robustness.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exploit symmetry: search over 3-fold symmetric and layered-boundary configurations
tried_paradigms.description: Known good Heilbronn configurations for small n place points on the boundary with symmetric structure. Restrict search to configurations invariant under the triangle's 120° rotation: orbits of size 1 (center) or 3. With 11 points, use e.g. orbits {3,3,3,1} or {3,3,3,2-ish boundary}, reducing dimensionality from 22 to ~8 free parameters (each orbit parameterized by one radial/edge parameter). Run dense multi-start local search (or the existing SA) in this low-dimensional space, plus variants with reflection symmetry. Low dimensionality allows near-exhaustive grid refinement to global optimality within the symmetry class, likely beating the unconstrained SA's local minimum. Also try 'onion' configurations: points on nested similar triangles.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Symmetric configs may be suboptimal vs asymmetric ones; test several orbit decompositions; keep tolerance 1e-6 for boundary points; verify all points inside triangle.

tried_paradigms.idea: Maximin LP-based local refinement: solve exact maximin area via iterative LP with constraint generation
tried_paradigms.description: The Heilbronn maximin problem can be attacked with a cutting-plane scheme: variables are the 22 point coordinates plus a slack variable t; constraints are linear inequalities |cross(p_i,p_j,p_k)| >= t for all 165 triplets (each absolute value gives two linear inequalities). Each iteration, solve a feasibility LP with the currently active constraints via scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS), add the most violated constraints, and repeat. Since areas are linear in each point's coordinates given the others, this converges to a local optimum of the true nonsmooth objective far more reliably than simulated annealing. Use multiple structured seeds (boundary-heavy layouts known good for n=11) and keep the best final t. Finish with a tiny greedy polish to fix numerical issues.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary), via exact linear-programming local optima
tried_paradigms.cautions: The absolute value makes constraints nonconvex jointly, so iterate: fix sign pattern of each triplet's cross product from the current iterate, solve LP, re-check signs, repeat. Use scipy.optimize.linprog with HiGHS for speed; cap iterations to stay within eval time; project points into the triangle with barycentric bounds as LP constraints (u,v>=0, u+v<=1).

tried_paradigms.idea: Nonsmooth gradient ascent with scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) on a soft-min objective
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the hard min over 165 areas with a smooth soft-min (log-sum-exp with temperature) and run scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP or trust-constr) on the negative objective over the 22 coordinates, with barycentric coordinate bounds (u,v >= 0, u+v <= 1) as linear constraints. Anneal the temperature: start with a soft min over many triplets, gradually sharpen so the optimizer focuses on the true bottleneck triangles. Multi-start from the current best configuration, structured boundary seeds, and random seeds; keep the best true min area. SLSQP handles the linear constraints exactly and converges quadratically near nonsmooth optima once the active set (bottleneck triangles) stabilizes.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized; escape the plateau behavior of the current coordinate-descent annealer
tried_paradigms.cautions: Log-sum-exp needs a temperature scaled to typical areas (~0.01-0.04); too small causes overflow/ill-conditioning, too large blurs the objective. Always evaluate the true hard min at the end. Provide analytic gradients (sum of weighted per-triangle gradients) for speed and reliability. Enforce a strict feasibility check with the evaluator's tolerance before returning.

tried_paradigms.idea: Known-optimum structural ansatz search: exploit symmetric boundary configurations with reduced parameterization
tried_paradigms.description: Best-known n=11 equilateral-triangle Heilbronn configurations place most points on the boundary (vertices plus edge subdivisions) with a small interior set, often with a 3-fold symmetry. Parameterize candidate layouts by a small number of degrees of freedom: k points per edge at unknown positions plus m interior points on the symmetry axis, and optimize only those few variables (e.g., 3-6 parameters) with a fine grid search followed by the existing local polish. Enumerate several structural families (all-on-boundary, one interior point on the axis, two interior symmetric points, etc.). Because the search space is tiny, exhaustive refinement reaches machine precision, and the structure guarantees feasibility and symmetry-balanced bottleneck triangles.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized via structural exploitation of known-good Heilbronn geometry
tried_paradigms.cautions: Verify each candidate with the exact evaluator formula (normalized by sqrt(3)/4). Grid search must be dense enough (>=1e-4 resolution) then refined. Keep the deterministic fallback of the current annealer if no structural candidate beats it. Symmetric layouts can have degenerate collinear triplets giving zero area — check all 165 triplets explicitly.
